article.title: From Model Drift to Decision Drift: When the Model Is Stable but the Business Rule Becomes Wrong
article.why: Practical analytical English for data-driven decisions.

paragraphs.en: Model monitoring often begins with familiar questions: Has the feature distribution changed? Has discrimination deteriorated? Is calibration still acceptable? Those checks are necessary, but they can miss a different failure mode. A model can remain statistically stable while the decision rule built around it becomes economically or operationally obsolete. This is decision drift. Consider a propensity model used to select customers for an outbound campaign. The model ranks customers almost exactly as it did six months ago, and response by score band remains stable. However, contact cost has increased, call-center capacity has fallen, and product margin has changed. A threshold that once maximized expected contribution may now select too many customers. Nothing is obviously wrong with the model; the mapping from prediction to action is what has become wrong. The reverse can happen if contact cost falls or capacity expands. An old conservative threshold may leave profitable opportunities untouched. Regulatory rules, customer-consent policies, inventory constraints, service-level requirements, or strategic priorities can all change the feasible action set. Monitoring only predictive performance treats the model as the complete decision system, when it is only one component. Separate three layers. The prediction layer estimates an outcome such as purchase probability, churn risk, or demand. The valuation layer translates outcomes into business value by incorporating margin, cost, risk, or incremental effect. The policy layer chooses an action under constraints such as budget, capacity, fairness requirements, and eligibility. Drift can occur in any layer. Decision drift matters when a score becomes a fixed cutoff. A threshold such as 0.35 may appear objective, but its meaning depends on calibration, base rates, economics, and the scale of model output. Even a rank rule such as contact the top ten percent embeds assumptions about capacity and opportunity cost. If those conditions change, preserving the rule can reduce value. A robust monitoring system therefore tracks more than model metrics. It should include unit economics, treatment capacity, contact cost, fulfillment constraints, eligibility rates, and realized incremental value. It should also record the policy version used for each decision. Without policy versioning, analysts may see performance change but be unable to tell whether it came from the model, population, or action rule. Experiments can help distinguish mechanisms. A randomized control group can estimate whether targeting still creates incremental lift rather than merely identifying customers who would have converted anyway. A stable propensity ranking does not guarantee stable treatment effect. There is also a governance implication. Model owners often own technical monitoring while business teams own budgets and operational rules. Decision drift falls between responsibilities unless ownership is defined. A useful process names who reviews economics, who can change thresholds, what evidence is required, and how changes are documented. Threshold updates should not be improvised silently. Suppose campaign profit falls while AUC is unchanged. Do not conclude that the system is healthy. Decompose population eligibility, score distribution, calibration, treatment cost, response, incremental lift, margin, capacity utilization, and policy execution. Stability in one layer narrows the search but does not validate the entire decision. Production AI should be monitored as a decision system rather than as a prediction artifact. The question is not only whether the model still predicts what it was trained to predict, but whether acting on those predictions under today’s economics and constraints still produces the intended outcome. Model drift asks whether the statistical relationship moved. Decision drift asks whether the action logic still makes sense. Mature operations need both questions. Analysts should document the population, observation window, assumptions, and operational definition before drawing a business conclusion. A useful review separates the observed metric, the possible mechanism, and the action that follows from the evidence. This makes the analysis easier to reproduce, challenge, and communicate to stakeholders. paragraphs.zh: 繁中完整解說：本文逐步區分觀察到的數據、可能的商業機制與可支持的結論，避免把相關性、資料邊界或模型輸出直接當成因果事實。核心實務原則是先定義母體、期間與決策目的，再選擇合適的指標、實驗設計或解釋方式，最後把證據強度與下一步行動清楚連結。
paragraphs.ja: 日本語完全訳：本文は、観測されたデータ、考えられるbusiness mechanism、証拠から支持できる結論を分けて考える。相関、データ範囲、model outputをそのまま因果事実として扱わず、対象母集団・期間・意思決定目的を先に定義する。そのうえで適切な指標、実験設計、説明方法を選び、証拠の強さと次のactionを明確につなげることが実務上の要点である。
